digest.component_or_area: file impact declaration and tri-state scope tracking
propositions: Empty file_impact value is overloaded and ambiguous: distinguishes between author forgetting to declare and an explicit no-file-impact statement, requiring consumers to assume conservative reading.
The data model must support three mutually exclusive states: undeclared (no declaration), none (explicit no-file-impact), and paths (non-empty file list), derived in one place by process_file_impact.
CLI command set-file-impact must support two exclusive forms: JSON array for paths and --none with a reason string, with reason validation requiring at least 10 non-whitespace characters.
New library function get_file_impact_scope returns dict with kind, reason, and paths; new MCP tool declare_no_file_impact applies identical reason validation and writes event.

Reducer state must track file_impact_scope (default undeclared) and no_file_impact_reason (default empty), with transition rules: non-empty file_impact yields paths, empty file_impact plus payload file_impact_scope=none yields none, otherwise undeclared.
Existing get-file-impact and next_batch surfaces remain unchanged; set-file-impact migrates from _REGISTRY to _ARGV_REGISTRY to support variadic argv parsing.
